summary: Dual-signal (BSE + SE) automated particle recognition, crystallographic facet fitting, and in-situ micro-compression stage navigation.

items.description: Moves the image viewport.
Zooms into or out of the cursor location.
Auto-ranges view to fit image bounds.
Toggles between Secondary Electron (SE) and Backscattered Electron (BSE) signals.
Runs multi-scale FFT cross-correlation to align all site images to the region overview.
Drag any site box on the overview image to manually adjust its stage offset.
Reverts the last manual site rectangle repositioning.
Switches to Site Analysis tab and displays the selected site.
Places a red crosshair marker at the particle location.
Sets the maximum bounding radius for outer particle recognition on BSE.
Chooses the top facet geometry before fitting (Hexagon, Triangle, Quad, Pentagon, 6-gon, 8-gon, Ellipse).
Fits outer boundary ellipse on BSE, auto-centers, and fits the chosen facet shape on SE.
Measures equivalent circular diameter on BSE signal without facet fitting.
Fits facet shape on SE using current center coordinates.
Advances sequentially to the next site in the dropdown and displays its particles.
Deletes selected particle row and removes its overlays.
Equiangular crystallographic hexagon with strictly locked 120.0° internal angles.
3-sided polygon for octahedral and tetrahedral {111} facets.
4-sided polygon for cubic {100}, tetragonal, or trapezoidal facets.
5-sided polygon for decahedral nanoparticle twins and pyritohedral {210} facets.
6-sided polygon with freely adjustable, unconstrained vertex angles.
8-sided polygon for truncated cuboctahedra and {100}+{110} facet projections.
Curvilinear facet model with independent major/minor semi-axes and rotation.
Scales and rotates the entire hexagon self-similarly around its geometric center (all 120° angles preserved).
Slides the dragged corner and its 2 adjacent vertices along the second-next edge directions (120° locked).
Slides the 2 endpoints strictly along adjacent edge rays, shortening or lengthening that edge (120° locked).
Translates the entire hexagon across the particle surface.
Moves only the dragged corner freely; all other corners remain strictly stationary.
Translates the entire polygon without altering vertex relative coordinates.
Scales the semi-major axis length.
Scales the semi-minor axis length.
Rotates ellipse orientation angle.
Translates the ellipse across the particle.
1-click combined outer particle + facet recognition.
Transitions between Ready for Test (Mode A) and Translation Guidance (Mode B), accepting stage moves and logging tests.
Removes selected particle measurement.
Saves session, particles, and facet parameters to sample_data.json.
Opens sample directory.
Reverts site position adjustment on region overview.
Opens this Help dialog.
Closes the application.
Toggles between Mode A (Ready for Test / Current Particle Confirmation) and Mode B (Stage Translation Guidance).
Displays large Current Particle UID, live test status, SE site confirmation view, and remaining test queue.
Shows Target Particle UID, target SE site preview with highlighted particle, and exact SmarAct ΔX, ΔY stage motion vector.
Accepts actual stage displacements, updates calibration, logs complete test record (ECD, facet, area, coordinates, timestamp) to JSON, and advances.
Setting a current particle automatically computes the shortest travel tour (Euclidean Nearest Neighbor) across all remaining particles and selects the next target.
Compensates for 70° sample tilt and arbitrary mounting rotation to match SEM viewport orientation.
Estimates stage rotation φ and scale s with analytical standard deviations (σ_φ, σ_s) and 1-hop RANSAC outlier rejection.
Displays continuous confidence percentage (⚡ Calibrated XX%) and switches to green once orientation is statistically certain.
Interactive stage scaling factor (µm/µm) that adapts future travel distance predictions based on observed piezo travel.

items.shortcut: Flip X/Y / Invert X / Invert Y
items.description: Instantly swaps or inverts piezo coordinate axes to match microscope stage wiring.
Unique short IDs formatted as {Site}_{ParticleID} (e.g., 2_23, 22_3, 6_1) for unambiguous identification and rapid note-taking.
Every test is recorded to compression_test_YYMMDDHH.json with full geometrical, positional, and calibration history for post-mortem analysis.
